title: muster release v5.28.2

### Fixed
- **A 429 on a session's initialize is a transient refusal, not a legacy SSE server.** When a remote MCP server answered a person's session initialize POST with `429 Too Many Requests` -- GitHub's hosted MCP server does when many tool calls of one session are in flight -- muster logged `failed to initialize MCP protocol: ... server returned 4xx for initialize POST, likely a legacy SSE server` and sent whoever read the log after a transport mismatch that was not there. mcp-go reduces every 4xx on the initialize POST to that one sentinel and drops the status; the per-session client (`DynamicAuthClient`, the person's grant, a forwarded or exchanged token) never typed it, so the connect failed with the generic message while the tool-call path already named the status. Now a 429 or 503 to the initialize is classified as retry-later on both connect paths: the client records the status and the `Retry-After` header off the wire and returns a typed `InitializeRefusedError` carrying both, the log and the CR status name the status (`endpoint answered the initialize POST with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests; retry after 1s`), the reconnect is scheduled for the `Retry-After` the server asked for rather than muster's doubling backoff, and the session's grant is kept so the next call reconnects. The generic 4xx message no longer claims a legacy SSE server for a status that has its own meaning -- `likely a legacy SSE server` is said only for the 405 that means it. The scenario `oauth-session-initialize-429-is-retry-later` answers one grant-adoption initialize with `429` and `Retry-After: 1`, and pins that the server stays connected, the log names the status without the legacy-SSE line, and the next tool call succeeds without a reconnect. ([#1303](https://github.com/giantswarm/muster/issues/1303))
